questions.q: Which of these is a parameter (learned during fit) rather than a hyperparameter?
options: max_depth of a decision tree
C of a logistic regression
The coefficients in coef_ of a fitted logistic regression
n_neighbors of a k-NN model
questions.explain: coef_ is computed by fit from the training data, so it is a learned parameter. The others are settings chosen before fit.

questions.q: In scikit-learn, how can you tell that an attribute was learned during fit?
options: It is set in the constructor
Its name ends with a trailing underscore, like coef_
It appears in get_params()
It starts with an underscore
questions.explain: By convention, attributes learned from data end in an underscore (coef_, intercept_, feature_importances_) and exist only after fit.

questions.q: A pipeline has steps named "scale" and "clf". How do you set the logistic regression's C to 0.1?
options: pipe.set_params(C=0.1)
pipe.set_params(clf.C=0.1)
pipe.set_params(clf_C=0.1)
pipe.set_params(clf__C=0.1)
questions.explain: Pipeline parameter names use the step name, two underscores, then the parameter name: clf__C.

questions.q: Why should you choose max_depth using cross-validation scores rather than training accuracy?
options: Training accuracy always favors the most complex model, even when it only memorizes
Training accuracy cannot be computed for trees
Cross-validation is faster to run
Training accuracy is always lower than validation accuracy
questions.explain: In the lesson, the unlimited tree scores 1.000 on training data. Only held-out scores show whether extra depth actually helps.

questions.q: In the lesson, max_depth=8 scored 0.916 (std 0.019) and max_depth=None scored 0.919 (std 0.024). How should you read that?
options: None is clearly better because 0.919 is higher
Depth 8 is clearly better because its std is lower
The difference is much smaller than the fold-to-fold spread, so they are effectively tied
Both scores are invalid because they used cross-validation
questions.explain: A gap of 0.003 is well inside the fold-to-fold noise of about 0.02, so the data do not distinguish the two settings.
